title: The nightly store run pauses for other work's memory, and the decision sets need less of it
request: The owner: fix the nightly store run's memory use.
spec: The scheduled store run is never lost to another job's memory: over 6 GB of swap it pauses and goes on under 5 GB, stops only after 3 hours paused or under 2 GB of disk, never leaves the run stopped, and logs how much the run itself held. The decision sets are built with a lower peak and the same content.
plan: read the nightly log: when and where each run was stopped
measure the decision builder's peak on the real store, stage by stage
pause instead of stop in the scheduler
one set at a time and compact placements in the builder
prove the same 189 sets by fingerprint

decisions.decision: Pause the run (SIGSTOP) instead of stopping it on swap
decisions.why: the stopped nights (11-19, 11-22) overlapped a 3-hour exam and the test gates; alone the run fits with swap about 3 GB, so waiting for the other work keeps four hours of progress

decisions.decision: Keep placements as (folder, quality) with shared strings, for the types the sets build
decisions.why: the builder reads only those two fields; 1.9 million whole dictionaries were its peak
what remains is the 370,000 decision records the sets need; reading them differently is a larger change for a smaller gain, and the pause covers the nights

change: scripts/store_scheduled.py guard, go_on, pause and resume; dclab_rnd/store/sets/decisions.py placements and per-set writing; tests.

findings.defect: the nightly store run was stopped on 11-19 and 11-22 and the store had no whole run from 11-18 to 11-22
findings.scenario: the swap guard stopped the run at 6 GB while other heavy work ran (the planning exam; the gates)
findings.cause: the guard stopped the run whatever held the memory
findings.fix: pause over 6 GB, go on under 5 GB, stop after 3 hours paused; log the run's own memory at each pause

findings.defect: the decision builder peaked at 2.66 GB
findings.scenario: measured on the real store: placements() held 1.9 million choices as dictionaries (2.2 GB) and every set's 686,771 examples were held to the end
findings.cause: whole dictionaries where two fields are read; all sets written at the end
findings.fix: (folder, quality) pairs of interned strings for the built types; one set built, written and let go at a time
findings.test: old and new builds on the real store: all 189 sets identical by sha256; peak 2.05 GB; test_placements_keep_only_folder_and_quality_for_the_types_the_sets_build

findings.defect: a paused run could be left stopped forever
findings.scenario: Ctrl-C or SIGTERM to the script while the run is paused: the child stays stopped, its exit-with-the-parent guard is a thread inside it, and every later night is refused as 'another store run is going'
findings.cause: no SIGCONT on the script's own exit
findings.fix: child.wait in try/finally that continues a paused child; a SIGTERM handler raising SystemExit (the previous handler restored)

findings.defect: an error in the watcher while paused left the run stopped and the script waiting forever
findings.scenario: sysctl failing to start under memory pressure while the run is paused
findings.cause: no finally in the watcher; the resume logged before it sent SIGCONT
findings.fix: the watcher's finally continues a paused child; SIGCONT before the log

measurements.name: decision builder on the real store, old against new
measurements.gate: every set identical; a lower peak
measurements.result: 189 of 189 sets identical by fingerprint; peak 2.66 to 2.05 GB; 173 s to 134 s

measurements.name: store tests and store-check
measurements.gate: every store test and the store's scripted day pass
measurements.result: 327 tests in 46 files OK; make store-check 30 of 30

outcome: A night with other heavy work now waits instead of losing the run; the builder peaks a quarter lower with the same sets.
lessons: Read when a guard fired against what else ran then before shrinking the guarded program.
Measure memory stage by stage: the obvious suspect (all examples held) was not the peak.
risks: A pause holds the run's memory (about 2 GB) while other work runs; macOS may swap it out.
Not yet seen on a real night.
